description: CATALOGUE-SRC-P1 external product research — 10 frozen SRC-P1 candidates. Research authorized by CATALOGUE-SRC-P0D acceptance (2026-09-10). This file contains factual product identity, composition, and positioning evidence only. NO final Maison metadata (collection, gender, family, vibe, occasion, character, season) has been assigned. All such assignments are deferred to a future governed editorial episode.

governance.p1rScope: LADIES-176 (Lacoste Rose identity disambiguation), LADIES-223 (Ultraviolet manufacturer/supplier status resolution), UNISEX-66 (Leather Malaki gender evidence — Malaki line pattern added)

sourcePolicyTiers.tier1: Official brand websites (brand product pages, official press releases) — AUTHORITATIVE
sourcePolicyTiers.tier2: Fragrantica.com, Basenotes.net, Parfumo.com, major authorised retailers (Nordstrom, Sephora, Harrods, FragranceNet) — HIGH

governance.admissibilityNote: LLM general knowledge is NOT admissible as a governed source. All claims must be traceable to a named external source. Fragrantica returns 403 on direct WebFetch — Fragrantica evidence comes from WebSearch snippets, classified HIGH rather than AUTHORITATIVE. Official brand pages accessed via direct WebFetch are classified AUTHORITATIVE. Official brand pages confirmed by WebSearch snippet (where direct access was blocked or redirected) are classified HIGH-AUTHORITATIVE_PARTIAL. Supplier product name alone is NOT factual metadata evidence.
governance.editorialExclusion: This research file does NOT assign Maison canonical metadata. The following fields are deferred to a future editorial episode: collection, gender (Maison canonical), family, vibe, occasion, scentCharacter, seasons, popularity, projection, bestSeller, merchandising. The evidenceStatus=READY in this file means research is complete — it does NOT authorise staging or promotion.
governance.commercialDistinctionRule: DISTINCT_FLANKER_ALLOWED=YES. SAME_EXISTING_IDENTITY_ALLOWED_AS_NEW=NO. The question is same-vs-distinct at the commercial identity level, not flanker-vs-original at the family level.

evidenceStatusKey.RESEARCH_COMPLETE: Identity, composition, and positioning evidence fully gathered from admissible sources. No unresolved blockers.
evidenceStatusKey.RESEARCH_PARTIAL: Evidence gathered but gaps remain — either official source inaccessible, identity ambiguity unresolved, or composition evidence incomplete.
evidenceStatusKey.RESEARCH_CONFLICTED: Evidence gathered but material conflicts between sources that cannot be silently resolved.
evidenceStatusKey.RESEARCH_BLOCKED: Research cannot proceed due to unresolvable prerequisite failure.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Rose Radiant Gold by Michael Kors, 2015 EDP, female. Part of Michael Kors Gold Collection. Official Michael Kors website (michaelkors.com) was accessed via search snippet — confirmed product name and EDP concentration but description is intentionally sparse: 'Tantalizing and hypnotic, Rose Radiant Gold entices the senses with notes of sparkling spice, textured with rich florals and subtle musks.' Official page redirected to regional site on direct WebFetch — full product page content not retrieved. Individual note names (bergamot, raspberry, rose, jasmine, peach) sourced from retailer descriptions (HIGH-tier range) only; not from official brand. Fragrantica page confirmed at https://www.fragrantica.com/perfume/Michael-Kors/Rose-Radiant-Gold-31342.html but returns 403 on direct WebFetch — note confirmation from Fragrantica search snippet only: 'top: Spices, middle: Floral Notes, base: Musk'. Gap signal: Rose×female depth — floral-forward character with rose and jasmine heart is consistent with evidence but not confirmed at AUTHORITATIVE tier. No MKC collision. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.sourceNotes: Official michaelkors.com description (confirmed by search snippet, HIGH-AUTHORITATIVE_PARTIAL): 'notes of sparkling spice, textured with rich florals and subtle musks'. Individual note pyramid (bergamot/raspberry/rose/jasmine/peach/musk) from retailer descriptions at https://www.perfume.com/michael-kors/michael-kors-rose-radiant-gold/women-perfume and https://luxuryperfume.com/collections/michael-kors/products/rose-radiant-gold-by-michael-kors — classified HIGH. Fragrantica search snippet confirms Spices/Floral/Musk scaffold. Note pyramid is plausible but not confirmed AUTHORITATIVE. Source tier: MIXED.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: L'Eau d'Issey Pour Homme Sport by Issey Miyake, 2012 EDT, male. Distinct flanker from L'Eau d'Issey Pour Homme (the original, already in MKC as leau-dissey-pour-homme-inspired). The Sport version has a spicier, heavier-bergamot profile vs the original's fresh yuzu/water-lily character. Perfumer Jacques Cavallier (same as original). Confirmed still available at multiple retailers as of 2025-2026 — not discontinued. Official Issey Miyake Parfums website (isseymiyakeparfums.com) fetched and read — the Sport variant is not listed in the current official lineup, but third-party retail availability confirms it remains commercially active. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY. Gap signal: Youthful×male, Energetic×male — citrus-spice character with sporting/dynamic positioning.
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): bergamot/grapefruit top; nutmeg/leather heart; vetiver/cedar/ambergris base. Perfumer confirmed Jacques Cavallier from Fragrantica snippet. Positioning: 'launched in 2012 as an energetic, unconventional edition ideal for everyday use' (Fragrantica news snippet). Described as spicier and heavier on bergamot than the original L'Eau d'Issey Pour Homme (which features yuzu/water lily). Official Issey Miyake Parfums page (isseymiyakeparfums.com) does not currently list the Sport variant; however, Walmart, FragranceNet, and ScentDecant carry it as of 2025-2026, confirming active commercial availability.
conflicts: Official Issey Miyake Parfums website does not list L'Eau d'Issey Pour Homme Sport in its current lineup, suggesting it may have been de-listed from the official product range. However, active third-party retail availability (Walmart, FragranceNet) as of 2025-2026 indicates the product remains commercially available. No discontinuation announcement found.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Leather Malaki by Chopard, 2024 EDP, marketed for men. Official Chopard product page fetched directly (AUTHORITATIVE). Notes, positioning, and concentration confirmed from official source. Perfumer Dora Baghriche confirmed from Fragrantica search snippet. GENDER CONFLICT: Supplier categorized UNISEX-66 but both official Chopard website (URL path: /perfume-for-men/) and Fragrantica classify Leather Malaki as a men's fragrance. The research does not confirm a unisex classification. This conflict must be resolved in a future editorial episode before canonical gender assignment. P1R ADDITIONAL GENDER EVIDENCE (2026-09-10): Chopard Malaki line pattern examined. Within the Malaki line: Rose Malaki (2014), Cedar Malaki (2023), Amber Malaki (2015), Black Incense Malaki (2020), and Musk Malaki (2017) are all classified as 'women and men' (unisex) by Fragrantica. By contrast, Oud Malaki (2012) and Leather Malaki (2024) are both classified as 'for men' only. This pattern indicates Chopard deliberately differentiates gender within the Malaki line — when they intend unisex positioning, they use that classification; Leather Malaki is deliberately marked male. This strengthens the recommendation that OFFICIAL_MALE_SHOULD_PREVAIL over the supplier's UNISEX classification. Gap signal: Leather×unisex — evidence supports leather/woody/spiced character, but official marketed gender is male (not unisex). SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.sourceNotes: Official Chopard product page (chopard.com/en-us/perfume-for-men/95201-0454.html) fetched directly — AUTHORITATIVE. Official description: 'Created for modern wayfarers who are irresistibly drawn to wide-open spaces and dizzying heights, Leather Malaki is an exhilarating, boundless breath of life.' Official notes: top bergamot essence and black pepper; heart Alaskan cedar essence (woody, spiced); base warm smoky notes / leathery-mineral accord. Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH) confirms same pyramid with added detail: Cedar, Cypress, Spicy Notes (heart); Leather, Labdanum, Mineral, Amber (base). Perfumer Dora Baghriche from Fragrantica snippet (HIGH). Size: 80ml. Price: USD 126.
entries.nameIssueExplanation: GENDER_CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT: Supplier categorized this entry as UNISEX-66, but official Chopard website lists Leather Malaki under the /perfume-for-men/ URL path and Fragrantica classifies it as 'a fragrance for men 2024'. The unisex classification in the supplier intake may reflect a supplier interpretation or error. A reviewer comment on Fragrantica notes it 'seems more unisex' but that is a community observation, not official brand positioning. Malaki line pattern (P1R 2026-09-10): five Malaki fragrances are officially unisex (Rose, Cedar, Amber, Black Incense, Musk); two are officially male-only (Oud, Leather) — Chopard deliberately distinguishes gender within this line. Evidence supports OFFICIAL_MALE_SHOULD_PREVAIL. The canonical Maison gender assignment must be decided in a future editorial episode with this conflict recorded.
conflicts: GENDER_CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT: Supplier category=UNISEX; official Chopard and Fragrantica classification=men's fragrance. Source: chopard.com (AUTHORITATIVE) and Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH).

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Roses de Chloé by Chloé, 2013 EDT, female. Distinct product from Chloé EDP (2008) which is already in MKC as chloe-original-inspired — different name, different year, different concentration, different note structure. Perfumers Michel Almairac and Mylène Alran confirmed from Fragrantica search snippet. Rich rose-dominant floral character with fruity softness (litchi, peach, apple). Gap signal: Rose×female depth — strong rose-forward floral with Damask Rose as primary heart note. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): litchi/bergamot/tarragon/lemon top; damask rose/magnolia/cedar/apple/black currant/peach heart; white musk/amber/woody base. Perfumers confirmed from Fragrantica snippet. Concentration EDT confirmed from Amazon listing and multiple retail sources. Fragrantica page: https://www.fragrantica.com/perfume/Chloe/Chloe-Roses-de-Chloe-18702.html (403 on direct WebFetch). No official Chloé brand page accessed directly.
entries.nameIssueExplanation: SUPPLIER_NAME_DISCREPANCY: Supplier wrote 'Chloe Roses' but canonical product name is 'Roses de Chloé' (reversed word order, accent on é). The identity is unambiguous — there is only one product matching this description. No commercial identity confusion.

entries.researchNotes: IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: The supplier name 'Lacoste Rose' does not uniquely identify a single Lacoste fragrance. P1R FINDINGS (2026-09-10): (1) Confirmed there is NO standalone 'Lacoste Rose' product outside the Lacoste L.12.12 Rose women's line — 'Lacoste Rose' unambiguously refers to the L.12.12 Rose sub-line. (2) The L.12.12 Rose line for women comprises at least six distinct products as of 2026: L.12.12 Rose Sparkling EDT (2015/2016, fruity/gourmand — NOT primarily rose-forward despite the name), L.12.12 Eau de Parfum Rose For Her (2021, rose/frangipani — most rose-forward and most prominently positioned), L.12.12 Rose Eau Fraîche (2022), L.12.12 Rose Eau Intense (2023), L.12.12 Silver Rose EDP (2025), and a new L.12.12 Rose EDP confirmed on lacoste.com as of 2026. (3) The supplier normalizationConfidence=LOW and identityNotes='' confirm the normalizer could not resolve which variant. (4) The other Lacoste ladies entries in the supplier catalogue use standalone product names ('Joy of Pink', 'Pour Femme', 'Touch of Pink') — no naming convention evidence distinguishes L.12.12 Rose variants. MOST PROBABLE MATCH: L.12.12 Eau de Parfum Rose For Her (2021) — the flagship rose-focused variant, most widely referenced as simply 'Lacoste Rose' in retail. Research conducted on this assumption. IDENTITY_VERDICT: IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS (remains unresolved — Founder/supplier confirmation of specific variant required). Lacoste official product pages returned 403. Notes and perfumers from Fragrantica search snippets (HIGH). No MKC collision. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY once identity is confirmed.
entries.canonicalName: L.12.12 Eau de Parfum Rose For Her
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): mint/green mandarin top; rose/frangipani heart; musk/ambrette base. Perfumers Marie Salamagne and Ane Ayo from Fragrantica snippet. Lacoste official product description from Lacoste search snippet (HIGH-AUTHORITATIVE_PARTIAL): 'reveals a radiant femininity with a floral fruity scent, with energizing green mandarin and fresh mint blending with musk and sweet rose for an elegant and enveloping feel.' Lacoste.com product page (LC007A01) returned 403 on direct WebFetch. CAUTION: research assumes the L.12.12 Rose EDP (2021) as the most probable match for 'Lacoste Rose' — Founder or supplier confirmation of specific variant required before staging.
entries.nameIssueExplanation: IDENTITY_DISAMBIGUATION_REQUIRED: Supplier name 'Lacoste Rose' matches the brand name of the Lacoste L.12.12 Rose women's fragrance line, but does not uniquely identify which variant (Sparkling, EDP, Eau Fraîche, Eau Intense, Silver Rose). Research assumes L.12.12 Rose EDP For Her (2021) as flagship/most likely. Founder confirmation of the specific intended product is required before this entry proceeds to staging.
conflicts: IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: 'Lacoste Rose' maps to the L.12.12 Rose women's sub-line (confirmed: no standalone Lacoste Rose exists outside this line). Within the line, at least six distinct products exist as of 2026. Research conducted on L.12.12 Rose EDP For Her (2021) as most probable match. Founder/supplier disambiguation required before staging.

MULTIPLE_LINE_VARIANTS: L.12.12 Rose Sparkling (2015/2016 EDT) is the earliest Rose variant — but notes are fruity/gourmand (not rose-forward: apple/spices/blackberry/mandarin/cotton candy/musk), making it less likely for a supplier using 'Rose' as the primary identity signal. A new L.12.12 Rose EDP was released on lacoste.com in 2026, adding an additional candidate.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Ultraviolet Woman by Rabanne (formerly Paco Rabanne), 1999 EDP, female. Notes well-established from multiple HIGH-tier sources. Brand rebranded from 'Paco Rabanne' to 'Rabanne' (the supplier name 'Paco Rabanne Ultra Violet' reflects the pre-rebrand brand name). Official Rabanne product page found (rabanne.com) but could not be fetched (socket hang-up). P1R MANUFACTURER STATUS RESOLUTION (2026-09-10): The P1 'DISCONTINUATION_RISK' concern is substantially mitigated by P1R follow-up. Multi-retailer availability confirmed: Amazon.com, Walmart, Jomashop, eBay, Perfumes Club, and Wafa International (duty-free, global shipping) all list Ultraviolet Woman EDP in multiple sizes (1.7oz, 2.7oz, 80ml) as of 2025-2026. The Fragrantica forum thread ('Is Ultraviolet being discontinued?') reflects community concern and some market-specific phase-outs, but actual retail availability remains strong. Manufacturer production status is UNCERTAIN (product may no longer be manufactured in its original capacity by Rabanne, or may be winding down in some markets) but this is distinct from supplier/retail availability which is CONFIRMED_AVAILABLE. The Maison supplier (August 2026 catalogue) lists it — CURRENTLY_LISTED. The previous RESEARCH_PARTIAL designation was driven by the unresolved discontinuation concern; that concern is now clarified at the SUPPLIER_AND_RETAIL level. MANUFACTURER_STATUS: UNCERTAIN. SUPPLIER_AVAILABILITY: CURRENTLY_LISTED. CATALOGUE_RESEARCH_ELIGIBILITY: ELIGIBLE_FOR_EDITORIAL_REVIEW. Factual product evidence (notes, perfumer, positioning) fully supported. Gap signal: Powdery×female, Spicy×female — violet/spice/patchouli character confirmed. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): apricot/coriander/orange pepper/red pepper/fresh almond/rosewood top; violet/Japanese osmanthus/rose/jasmine heart; vanilla/amber/patchouli/cedar base. Perfumer Jacques Cavallier from Fragrantica snippet. Positioning from Fragrantica snippet: 'oriental floral fragrance that feels invisible yet ultra-sensory, just as an emotion.' Official Rabanne page (https://www.rabanne.com/ww/en/fragrance/p/ultraviolet-woman--000000000065051816) found via search but returned socket hang-up on WebFetch — classified HIGH-AUTHORITATIVE_PARTIAL (URL confirmed from official domain). Launch year: Fragrantica says 1999; one search snippet says 2000 — minor discrepancy; 1999 used as most widely cited.
entries.nameIssueExplanation: DUAL_ISSUE: (1) Supplier wrote 'Ultra Violet' (two words) but canonical name is 'Ultraviolet' (one word). (2) Supplier wrote 'Paco Rabanne' but the brand rebranded to 'Rabanne' — canonical brand is now 'Rabanne'. Neither issue creates commercial identity ambiguity; the product is clearly identifiable.
conflicts: MANUFACTURER_STATUS_UNCERTAIN: Rabanne Ultraviolet Woman may no longer be in active production in some markets (Fragrantica forum thread and eBay 'Discontinued' category both suggest wind-down in certain regions). However, strong multi-retailer availability (Amazon, Walmart, Jomashop, eBay, Perfumes Club, Wafa International) as of 2025-2026 confirms retail stock remains available. Official Rabanne page (rabanne.com) confirmed via URL but could not be fetched for production status verification. RESOLUTION: Supplier (August 2026 catalogue) lists it as CURRENTLY_LISTED — supplier availability is confirmed. Manufacturer production uncertainty does not block editorial review.
LAUNCH_YEAR_MINOR_CONFLICT: Fragrantica lists 1999; one retailer search snippet lists 2000. Fragrantica (HIGH) used as primary — 1999 recorded.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: 212 VIP Rosé by Carolina Herrera, 2014 EDP, female. Official Carolina Herrera product page fetched directly (AUTHORITATIVE). Notes, positioning, concentration, and perfumers confirmed from official source. Distinct from 212 VIP Black (already in MKC as 212-vip-black-inspired) — different name, different year, different character. Also distinct from 212 Heroes (212-heroes-inspired, male). Gap signal: Rose×female depth — rose/peach blossom heart with champagne rosé sparkle character. Floral Fruity Woody family confirmed. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.perfumer: Lucas Sieuzac, Quentin Bisch, Emilie Coppermann

Official description: 'Fresh, sparkling and feminine, this fruity floral Eau de Parfum blends Champagne Rosé, peach blossom and roses, in a luminous rosé bottle.' Official positioning: 'celebrations, evenings out, special occasions'; personality: 'Glamourous & Magnetic'. Perfumers Lucas Sieuzac, Quentin Bisch, Emilie Coppermann confirmed from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH). Olfactive family Floral Fruity Woody confirmed from official page.
entries.nameIssueExplanation: SUPPLIER_NAME_DISCREPANCY: Supplier wrote '212 VIP Rose' but canonical product name is '212 VIP Rosé' (accent on the é). The identity is unambiguous. The accent should be preserved in the canonical name and proposed slug should use the unaccented version for ASCII slug compatibility.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Cool Water Woman by Davidoff, 1996 EDT, female. Official Davidoff product page fetched directly (AUTHORITATIVE). Distinct commercial identity from Davidoff Cool Water for Men (1988), which is already in MKC as cool-water-inspired (gender=male, Skye, Travel occasions). Female product has entirely different composition — aquatic/floral character vs male's fougère/spicy character. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY (DISTINCT_FLANKER_ALLOWED=YES applies — female flanker of the Cool Water family). COOL_WATER_TRAVEL_EVIDENCE: Official Davidoff positioning is 'fresh aquatic' with 'warm-weather occasions' — no explicit travel language in official sources. Classification: RELATED_POSITIONING_ONLY. The gap signal for Travel×female remains EXPLORATORY. The fresh/aquatic/warm-weather character is consistent with potential travel association but this is an editorial observation, not a confirmed source fact.
entries.sourceNotes: Official Davidoff product page (zinodavidoff.com/fragrances/cool-water-woman-eau-de-toilette-100-ml) fetched directly — AUTHORITATIVE. Official description: 'A fresh aquatic fragrance that reinforces a woman's confident beauty. Enjoy this glistening of water over skin, the utmost fresh sensuality.' Official notes (simplified): top watermelon and pineapple; heart lily of the valley; base blackcurrant and sensual woods. Extended note pyramid from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): full pyramid recorded in topNotes/heartNotes/baseNotes. Perfumer Pierre Bourdon from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH). Official Davidoff positioning for occasion: 'everyday wear, morning routines, the office, warm-weather occasions or casual evenings'. Travel language: NOT present in official sources. Aquatic/fresh/warm-weather character is noted as SOURCE_FACT. Travel editoral signal is EDITORIAL_OBSERVATION only.
conflicts: NOTE_DETAIL_TIER_DIFFERENCE: Official Davidoff page (AUTHORITATIVE) lists simplified notes (watermelon/pineapple/lily-of-the-valley/blackcurrant/sensual woods). Fragrantica (HIGH) provides the full expanded pyramid. Both are recorded; simplified official version is primary authority.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: La Nuit Trésor Nude by Lancôme, 2020 EDT, female. Distinct commercial identity from La Nuit Trésor (EDP, 2015 original) which is already in MKC as la-nuit-tresor-inspired. The Nude version is a lighter EDT flanker with a significantly simplified note structure (bergamot/rose/vanilla/coconut vs the original's more complex rose/blackcurrant/amber/iris pyramid). Launched January 2020. Lancôme brand positions it as 'gracious and feminine interpretation' with 'contrasts of romantic rose notes and some sunny accords, warm and pleasant, like a kiss on the skin.' Gap signal: Powdery×female — warm vanilla/coconut base with rose suggests warmth; note structure is lighter and more casual than the original. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY (DISTINCT_FLANKER_ALLOWED=YES).
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): bergamot top; rose heart; vanilla/coconut base. Confirmed by multiple retailer search snippets consistent with Fragrantica. Lancôme official description sourced via search snippet (HIGH-AUTHORITATIVE_PARTIAL): 'La Nuit Trésor Nude shows the contrasts of romantic rose notes and some sunny accords, warm and pleasant, like a kiss on the skin.' Launched January 2020, available in 30ml/50ml/100ml EDT. Lancôme USA product page (lancome-usa.com) returned 403 on direct WebFetch. No perfumer identified from available sources.

entries.researchNotes: Identity confirmed: Polo Sport by Ralph Lauren, 1994 EDT, male. Perfumer Harry Fremont confirmed from Fragrantica snippet. Distinct from Polo Black (polo-black-inspired) and Polo Blue (polo-blue-inspired) already in MKC — Polo Sport is an older, distinct product with a different aromatic/aquatic character. The brand also released 'Polo Sport Fresh' (2021) as a modern reinterpretation, but the supplier entry 'Polo Sport' clearly refers to the original 1994 EDT. Official Ralph Lauren Fragrances page (ralphlaurenfragrances.com) returned 403. Gap signal: Youthful×male, Energetic×male — widely described as sporty, aquatic, youthful; 'ideal for athletes or sports-minded men'; 'perfect for wearing at school and to extracurricular activities.' Fresh/aquatic character with mint/citrus/lavender opening. SAME_VS_DISTINCT: DISTINCT_COMMERCIAL_IDENTITY.
entries.sourceNotes: Notes from Fragrantica search snippet (HIGH): full pyramid confirmed. Perfumer Harry Fremont from Fragrantica snippet. Character from multiple search sources: 'Aromatic Green fragrance for men'; 'fresh, aquatic character'; 'youthful and aquatic'; 'sporty, casual'; 'ideal for athletes or sports-minded men'; 'perfect for wearing at school and to extracurricular activities'. Official Ralph Lauren Fragrances page (ralphlaurenfragrances.com) returned 403. Basenotes.com listing confirmed at https://basenotes.com/fragrances/polo-sport-by-ralph-lauren.26121307. Note: Polo Sport Fresh (2021) is a distinct modern reinterpretation — the supplier entry refers to the original 1994 Polo Sport.
